note: A task model is a trained policy/skill pack for a specific physical job. Hardware capability is not enough. Do not call these certificates in product UI.
honesty: Chat LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, Mistral) are not warehouse pick, hospital logistics, or CNC tending policies. Search vision-language-action families and OEM packs. Token API prices are not robot-policy prices. Field traces do not automatically cut the model price.

model_layers.label: Foundation VLA / generalist policy
model_layers.note: OpenVLA, π0.5, GR00T, Octo, ACT, LeRobot. Pretrained on many robots and tasks. Not qualified for this workplace. Distributors do not train this layer.

model_layers.label: Task library / skill pack
model_layers.note: OEM application store: warehouse pick, hospital linen, floor scrub, kitchen dish. Specific libraries for specific tasks. Usually licensed, not trained from scratch by the distributor.

model_layers.label: Site-adapted policy
model_layers.note: Fine-tune or program this floorplate, SKU mix, fixture, SOP. This is the unpaid hole when a channel only resells the chassis.

training_time_bands.label: Days to ~2 weeks
training_time_bands.meaning: Install and license an existing OEM pack; mapping and smoke test. Not greenfield training.

training_time_bands.label: 1–4 weeks
training_time_bands.meaning: Site map, coverage program, or a small fine-tune when demonstration traces already exist.

training_time_bands.label: 2–8 weeks
training_time_bands.meaning: Collect demos, fine-tune, evaluate, and qualify on this cell. Typical pick/AMR adapt.

training_time_bands.label: 4–12 weeks
training_time_bands.meaning: Custom cell, fixture, clinical SOP, or kitchen menu. Integrator SOW, not a download.

training_time_bands.label: Months to years
training_time_bands.meaning: Foundation VLA pretrain. Lab/OEM compute. Not the distributor's job.

data_contract.summary: The robot company or distributor must bring workplace evidence. A SKU URL is not enough to train or qualify a policy.

you_provide.label: Site map / layout
you_provide.examples: CAD, BIM, fleet map, aisle widths, keep-out zones

you_provide.label: Work objects
you_provide.examples: SKU list, tote/case dimensions, payload, fixture drawings, menu/dish mix

you_provide.label: Demonstration traces
you_provide.examples: Teleop or human videos of the successful task; hours of episodes, not a brochure

you_provide.label: Failure cases
you_provide.examples: Drops, collisions, occlusions, night-shift lighting, wet floors

you_provide.label: SOP and safety envelope
you_provide.examples: Who shares the aisle, infection-control rules, e-stop, payload limits

you_do_not_owe: A foundation VLA pretrain dataset — that is the lab/OEM layer
Invented wages or FTE economics for the Job Card

pricing_contract.honesty: Do not invent dollars. Token API list prices are not OEM pack prices and not GPU hours for a cell policy.

who_pays.typical: Research weights are often free; commercial use needs a license. Training this layer is not a distributor line item.
OEM quotes a pack per robot, per site, or per fleet. Usually not on a public price list.
Integrator SOW is often the largest cost. Channel partners who only resell hardware leave this unpaid.

field_feedback.note: In-field traces usually improve the OEM's library, not the customer's invoice. A price cut happens only if the contract says so (data-for-license, reduced support, or a written rebate). Do not promise a discount because the robot learned on site.

qualify_filters.label: Is it a robot policy (VLA / OEM pack), not a chat LLM?
qualify_filters.note: OpenVLA, π0.5, Octo, LeRobot, ACT, GR00T N1.5, or an OEM application pack. GPT/Claude/Gemini/Llama text APIs do not pick cases or run hospital linens.

qualify_filters.label: Does the license allow commercial placement?
qualify_filters.note: Research-only and non-commercial CC licenses cannot put a robot into paid work. Check the model card before a distributor quotes a job.

qualify_filters.label: Can it run on this robot, on-prem, or only in the cloud?
qualify_filters.note: On-robot / edge work prefers small or quantized policies (often under ~8B parameters, or an OEM stack). Cloud VLMs are not the cell policy. Physical AI also pays simulation + always-on inference, not one pretrain run.

qualify_filters.label: Does context match the job (site map, video, long SOP)?
qualify_filters.note: Huge context windows matter for long video or documents. A pick cell still needs the motor policy, not a 1M-token chat window.

qualify_filters.label: Has it been qualified on this workplace?
qualify_filters.note: A downloaded checkpoint is not a site-qualified warehouse or hospital policy until that site says so.

pricing_lookups.name: BenchLM LLM pricing
pricing_lookups.note: Pay-per-token / image API list prices. Useful for managed VLMs. Not a price for an OEM warehouse pack or a trained cell policy.

pricing_lookups.name: Axe Compute — physical AI compute stack
pricing_lookups.note: Why robot policies cost more than LLMs: simulation, synthetic data, VLA training, and continuous on-robot inference. Quote GPU hours here — do not invent a dollar figure.

pricing_lookups.name: Vertex AI Model Garden
pricing_lookups.note: Google Gemini plus curated open models, billed per token/image. Not a robot cell license.

pricing_lookups.name: Amazon Bedrock
pricing_lookups.note: Unified API pricing for Claude, Llama, Titan, and others. Filter by use case; still not a warehouse pick policy.

pricing_lookups.name: Azure AI Foundry
pricing_lookups.note: OpenAI frontier models plus enterprise open-source. Pay-per-token. Does not qualify a hospital AMR.

pricing_lookups.name: Databricks Foundation Model APIs
pricing_lookups.note: Hosted FM pay-per-token on Databricks. Orientation for cloud cost, not physical-task pricing.

pricing_lookups.name: OEM application / fleet license quote
pricing_lookups.note: Usually not on a public price list. Ask the OEM what the task pack costs for this SKU.

pricing_lookups.name: Integrator cell / site-program SOW
pricing_lookups.note: Custom training and fixture programs are often the largest line item. Distributors who only resell hardware leave this unpaid.

shared_lookups.name: OpenVLA

shared_lookups.name: Physical Intelligence π0.5
shared_lookups.note: VLA with open-world generalization (April 2025). Not a site-qualified warehouse or hospital pack.

shared_lookups.name: NVIDIA GR00T N1.5
shared_lookups.note: Open foundation VLA for generalist humanoid robots (NVIDIA GEAR). Weights on Hugging Face. Presence on a candidate is unknown.

shared_lookups.name: Hugging Face robotics models
shared_lookups.note: Filter by robotics tasks. Then search OpenVLA, Octo, LeRobot. Presence on a candidate is unknown until named.

shared_lookups.name: Hugging Face — OpenVLA checkpoints
shared_lookups.note: Downloadable OpenVLA weights. The project page is the canonical lookup; this is the checkpoint index.

shared_lookups.name: LeRobot on Hugging Face
shared_lookups.note: Open robotics datasets and policies for download, fine-tune, and self-host.

shared_lookups.name: Argo-Robot foundation models for manipulation
shared_lookups.note: Survey of imitation-learning manipulation FMs (ACT, Octo, OpenVLA, Helix). Research map, not a storefront.

shared_lookups.name: Foundation models in robotics (Robocloud)
shared_lookups.note: Orientation on robotics foundation models. Not a catalog of site-qualified policies.

shared_lookups.name: Papers with Code — robotics / manipulation
shared_lookups.note: Academic leaderboards mapped to code and weights. Best-on-benchmark ≠ qualified on this workplace.

shared_lookups.name: GitHub — foundation-model codebases
shared_lookups.note: Cutting-edge weights often land here before commercial platforms. Search Awesome Foundation Models / Awesome robotics VLAs.

shared_lookups.name: Robotic Data
shared_lookups.note: Real-world Physical AI training data (LiDAR, human/task traces). A dataset is not a site-qualified warehouse or hospital policy. Do not invent a dataset price.

shared_lookups.name: World Labs — real-to-sim-to-real (SceniX)
shared_lookups.note: Train and evaluate robot policies in reconstructed scenes, then transfer back to the physical cell. Simulation success is not workplace qualification.

shared_lookups.name: Mercor
shared_lookups.note: People who can train, fine-tune, or host a robot policy. This is who builds the task model — not SIGNAL buyers and not a price list.
